@placement.scaled: {scale} is a plain number such as 1.0025, shown unchanged
placement.north_turned: The map's north is turned {degrees, number, 0.##}°.
placement.moved: The map is moved {meters, number, 0.##} m {direction, select, east {east} west {west} north {north} other {south}}.
@placement.moved: {direction} is one of east, west, north, south and chooses the word: keep these in English
placement.fitted: The map is fitted: north turned {degrees, number, 0.##}°{scaled, select, yes {, scale {scale, number, 0.#####}} other {}}.
@placement.fitted: {scaled} is yes or no and chooses a part of the sentence: keep it in English
@placement.reference_at: {where} is a place in the map written by placement.describe
placement.reference_middle: The reference point is the middle of tile {x}, {y}.
@placement.reference_lies: {latitude} and {longitude} are decimal degrees written with a point, shown unchanged
placement.describe: tile {x}, {y}, {east, number, 0.#} m east and {north, number, 0.#} m north of its south-west corner
placement.follow: The pictures shown follow it for now; load them again to cut them anew.
placement.own: This map lies on the Earth by itself.
placement.first: Place the map first: find the place and click on the map of the world.
placement.pick_reference: Click the map where the reference point is: it stays where it is on the Earth.
placement.pick_point: Click the map where point {n} is.
placement.point: Point {n} is {where}. Paste where it lies on the Earth.
placement.not_position: That is not a position: write the latitude and the longitude, like 52.5200, 13.4050.
placement.pick_both: Pick both points in the map first.
placement.paste_both: Paste the position of both points: latitude and longitude, like 52.5200, 13.4050.
placement.too_close: The two points lie too close together, in the map or on the Earth, to fit the map.
